issues.description: The problem text instructs students to initialize the SealSaloon attributes (including the shared stock) in the SealSaloon constructor, but elsewhere also requires the stock attribute to be static and final. Initializing a static final field in an instance constructor is incorrect/unusual and will confuse students (and is not what the provided solution does). The solution declares and initializes the static final stock at its declaration. This is a structural contradiction between the initialization guidance and the static/final requirement.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the instructions: either (A) require stock to be an instance (non-static) final field initialized in the constructor, or (B) keep stock static final and instruct students to initialize it at the point of declaration or in a static initializer. Update the problem statement to reflect the chosen approach (the solution uses a static final field initialized at declaration).

issues.description: The UML and problem specification show acceptSupplyDelivery as a public method (+acceptSupplyDelivery), but the solution declares acceptSupplyDelivery with package-private visibility (no 'public' modifier). This visibility mismatch between the spec and the implementation may confuse students about the expected API (whether the method should be public).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the visibility consistent: either change the solution to declare acceptSupplyDelivery as public static void acceptSupplyDelivery(...) or update the problem/UML to indicate package-private visibility. Prefer declaring the method public in the API specification and in the implementation to match the UML's '+' visibility.
